newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam lashes out at enemies in Christmas message.
newsitem.headline: Saddam lashes out at enemies in Christmas message.

text.p: President Saddam Hussein, in a Christmas and New Year message to Iraqi Christians, lashed out at Iraq's enemies and said his party's revolution had united Moslems and Christians.
He said the 1980-88 Iraq-Iran war and the 1991 Gulf War were launched against Iraq because its people were united despite their different religions.

"The episodes of murder and destruction (against the Iraqi people) started since the Iranian aggression in 1980 and then followed by the 33-nation aggression in mother of all battles (Iraq's nickname for the 1991 Gulf War)," Saddam said in a message broadcast by all Iraqi state-run media and read by Iraq's Culture and Information Minister Hamed Youssef Hummadi.

In his message Saddam cursed those who launched the Gulf War in 1991 which ejected Iraqi troops out of Kuwait and called them "the wicked". Saddam made no direct mention of the United States which led the war against his country.
The Iraqi president also lashed out at those whom he said were imposing the U.N. trade sanctions on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"After the mother of all battles, the episode of mass killing starts...(by) using new a weapon...and a new method that is the embargo," Saddam said.

He made no mention of the start of Iraq's oil exports to international markets two weeks ago under an oil-for-food deal signed with the United Nations in May. Under the pact Baghdad is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy urgent needs for the Iraqi people.
He said the July 1968 revolution which brought the ruling Baath Party to power has worked since its early days to unite the Iraqi people.
"July Revolution has helped the sons of Iraq to live together enjoying their different religions," Saddam said.
